items.summary: MIT researchers have developed a system that acts like an AI copilot, helping engineers collaboratively create structurally optimized designs through topology optimization. Traditionally, this method requires heavy computation and hides its reasoning in a black box, making outputs impractical to manufacture or difficult for engineers to trust—often prompting redesigns from scratch. The new approach uses machine learning trained on synthetic human feedback data to surface likely modification regions during generation, giving designers agency over the evolving design. In demonstrations, it improved manufacturability and linear buckling load by 39% while adding only modest time compared to fully algorithmic methods. Lead author Dat Ha PhD '26 now works at LeMessurier; co-authors include Ferdous Alam (Georgia Tech), Markus Buehler, Faez Ahmed, and Josephine Carstensen of MIT. The work was supported by the MathWorks Engineering Fellowship Fund, TATA Steel, and the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium.
items.title: MIT researchers build AI copilot for algorithmic structural design

items.summary: The reported affair between ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, suspected of spying for China, has triggered bipartisan national-security concerns in Washington. Schumer questioned what Trump knew when inviting Huang aboard Air Force One to Beijing; Jeffries demanded a classified briefing; Senate banking chair Tim Scott said he would consider subpoenaing Huang. Commerce secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to testify over his department's oversight of Nvidia exports and refusal to blacklist Chinese firms. House Speaker Mike Johnson noted growing consensus on limiting chip exports, with lawmakers pressing at least four bills. As China pursues domestic alternatives through Huawei amid weaker training efficiency, Chinese social media mourned the end of an era lasting decades.
items.title: Nvidia scandal sparks US national security furore and calls to take tough line on China

items.summary: Despite fears of robots replacing humans, Robust AI designs machines that augment human strengths in warehouses and factories. Its mobile robot Carter features a force-sensitive handlebar, vision system, and holonomic wheels for one-handed guidance. Co-founders Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92 and Rodney Brooks emphasize combining robotic, human, and backend work so people retain agency. The company targets the majority of unautomated facilities rather than rare fully automated systems costing $50 to $200 million each. Robots can be phased in gradually across several workflows.
items.title: Robust AI Builds Robots That Complement Human Workers

items.summary: Palm oil producers tied to October transboundary haze posted higher third-quarter 2026 profits in separate updates on Nov 13. First Resources saw underlying net profit rise 40.1% to US$122.7 million, with sales up 24.9% and EBITDA climbing 26.6%, though rupiah depreciation offset gains; it expects Indonesia's biodiesel programme and Middle East crude prices to support demand. Bumitama reported a modest 1.9% net profit increase but stronger nine-month results of 30.6%. Both firms cite productivity gains, reaffirm zero-burning commitments, and flag dry-weather fire risks in Kalimantan.
items.title: Haze-linked palm oil firms First Resources and Bumitama report higher Q3 profits

items.summary: WIRED's Uncanny Valley reports that Nvidia cofounder and former CEO Jensen Huang has officially resigned after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, compounded by a second reported affair with a direct report. The board turned on the founder despite his hard-fought resistance, installing CFO Colette Kress—who joined in 2013—as interim leader amid a search for a new visionary CEO. Nvidia's stock plunged but had been stabilizing as of recording. Barrett estimates Huang owns about 3.5 percent and led roughly 60 direct reports without a succession plan; he'd spoken of staying decades, having built the company over more than three decades from Denny's in the late 1990s. The episode frames this as an unusual moment for accountability at a founder-dominated firm, with implications for China relations, competitors diversifying their silicon stacks, and broader economic concentration.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal; Colette Kress Named Interim CEO

items.summary: ST Engineering reported third-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year on year to September, with nine-month revenue reaching $10 billion (+10%). Defence led the period at ~$4.3 billion (+7%), while commercial aerospace rose 12% to ~$4.1 billion and urban solutions/satellite grew 15% to ~$1.7 billion. The group declared a five-cent interim dividend, bringing nine-month payouts to 14 cents per share. Operating expenses fell to a record-low 9% of revenue, the order book hit $37.7 billion, and shares rose 0.2% to close at $9.76.
items.title: ST Engineering posts record Q3 revenue and declares interim dividend

items.summary: Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, President Donald Trump floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook as his successor via a Truth Social post declaring 'A Legend replaces a Legend!' Cook stepped down from Apple's CEO role on September 1, 2026 after 15 years, becoming executive chairman of the board. Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld independently suggested Cook in a Time op-ed.
items.title: Trump Floats Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's Successor at Nvidia

items.summary: Nvidia's co-founder and 33-year CEO Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO, and board member amid reports of affairs with a Chinese spy and an employee. CFO Colette Kress leads the company worth about $3.8 trillion until a successor is named.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns from Nvidia; Colette Kress Named Interim CEO

items.summary: Block has built Buzz, an open source collaboration workspace where employees and AI agents work together in channels, threads, and direct messages. Rather than committing to a single model for every workflow, users can create specialized agents—each backed by its own frontier or open-weight model from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Databricks—and bring them into shared conversations alongside colleagues. Buzz is model-agnostic and self-hostable. Block uses Databricks Unity Gateway as the centralized access layer to a broad selection of models through one integration. Engineers are experimenting with multi-agent configurations—such as using a capable coordinating agent over smaller efficient ones—and an internal benchmarking approach, reflecting a shift from single-model performance toward combining models, harnesses, and agents for each task.
items.title: How Block Powers Collaborative AI Agents with Buzz and Unity Gateway

items.summary: Ministry of Manpower (MOM) takes a serious view of work pass offences, including false declarations and illegal deployment of migrant workers. When investigating, MOM adopts a holistic approach considering each case's circumstances and individual culpability. Some workers may have been misled into unlawful arrangements while others knowingly participated; where needed, MOM works with partners like the Migrant Workers' Centre to assist affected migrants.
items.title: MOM Investigates Work Pass Offences While Protecting Deceived Workers

items.summary: First Dog on the Moon introduces Pino, an autonomous virtual kiwi who independently decides his own preferences and actions rather than following preset programming. The cartoon character has chosen to be interested in trains and cats, illustrating a playful exploration of what a self-directed artificial personality might look like. First Dog promotes its cartoons via email signup and sells related merchandise through its shop.
items.title: A Virtual Kiwi Named Pino Makes His Own AI Decisions

items.summary: Solar module maker Heliene, together with perovskite company Caelux, has announced commercial-scale production of perovskite/silicon tandem modules at its facility in Minnesota. The product layers Caelux's Energy Producing Glass over a traditional silicon module to reach efficiencies of 27% or more, using four-terminal (4T) technology that keeps the two light-absorbing layers as independent circuits. Heliene chose this architecture and domestic manufacturing for integration ease; commercial shipments are expected in 2027 under a long-term multi-gigawatt agreement targeting 29% efficiency by 2028.
items.title: Heliene and Caelux Begin Commercial Production of Perovskite Tandem Solar Modules in Minnesota

items.summary: Crude oil prices were on course for a second weekly loss after two days of gains amid mixed signals from the Middle East. Brent traded at $95.87 and WTI at $88.49 per barrel, well below mid-October peaks but above pre-war February levels. Iranian attacks on Hormuz tankers continued, with reports that four vessels were targeted for noncompliance. Saudi Arabia said crude production rebounded to 10.56 million barrels daily last month.
items.title: Oil Prices Head for Second Weekly Loss Despite Middle East Attacks

items.summary: Senior White House officials reportedly are considering removing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid criticism over his handling of export controls and the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Scrutiny intensified after Huang resigned Thursday following reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Questions focus on whether Lutnick's department prevented advanced Nvidia AI chips from reaching China via Megaspeed.
items.title: Nvidia chip row: White House mulls ouster of Howard Lutnick over handling of export controls, Huang scandal

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams scheduling, and Exchange-based services for OpenAI, Anthropic, IndiGo, Akasa Air, Taiwanese firms, and Australian businesses. Microsoft ruled out a cyber-attack, citing server overload from a recent configuration change, while governments warned of productivity losses, scam risk, and reliance on single providers.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Businesses Across Australia and Taiwan

items.summary: After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid scandal, Chinese investors dumped shares in US-facing AI model and hardware firms on Nov 13. Fears of tighter US chip export controls—possibly by year-end—and a more skeptical Congress weighed heavily. Domestic chipmakers like Cambricon rose as bets shifted toward self-reliance.
items.title: Chinese AI Shares Tumble After Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resigns

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO of Nvidia after more than 30 years, having grown it from a $1bn firm at its 1999 IPO to over $4tn in 2026. The ouster followed revelations of an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect is a Chinese spy and top executive at Megaspeed. China denied the accusations as a smear.
items.title: Timeline of the Affair Scandal That Sank Nvidia's Jensen Huang

items.summary: अक्टूबर 2026 में भारत की खुदरा महंगाई दर 6.09% तक बढ़ गया, जो सितंबर (5.54%) और RBI की तय ऊपरी सीमा 6% दोनों के पार है। यह जनवरी 2026 के 2.74% से लगातार नव्वे महीने तक बढ़ोतरी है और नई CPI सरीज़ (आधार वर्ष 2024) का सबसे ऊँचा स्तर है। इसलिए दिसंबर में RBI की मौद्रिक नीति समीक्षा पर बाजऱ की नजर रहेगी।
items.title: भारत में अक्टूबर की महंगाई RBI की ऊपरी सीमा पार कर गई

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 13), Australia's spy agency, the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation, and federal police were among organisations affected by a global outage of Microsoft programmes. Users worldwide could not access services for hours, including Microsoft 365, Outlook and Teams. ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess and AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett confirmed their agencies were impacted. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft told him the outage was not caused by a cyber attack, and that an agreement he signed on Australia's behalf with Microsoft had been activated to prioritise restoration of Australian services.
items.title: Australia's ASIO and AFP Hit by Microsoft Outage

items.summary: The likely ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may slow ambitious AI buildouts in the Gulf, where local champions like PIF-owned HUMAIN and Abu Dhabi-backed G42 compete hard for US chip access amid China-diversion fears. Lawmakers push new curbs on chip diversion that could threaten development speed. Still, the region's customer-vendor relationship with Nvidia remains strong; investor Hussain Sajwani calls it "the most important company today in the world," warning a leader departure would be a big loss.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Fallout Could Slow Gulf AI Buildout

items.summary: A crisis at Nvidia reversed a brief AI-led stocks rally and intensified fears of a bursting tech bubble. Markets in South Korea and Taiwan fell, while Nvidia shares declined 6% in premarket trading as the world's most valuable company. Concerns have mounted over growing tech-sector borrowing, circular financing, and whether revenues will keep pace with historic capex plans. The potential ouster of Nvidia's CEO risks deepening these worries.
items.title: Nvidia scandal hits tech stocks

items.summary: Jersey's States adopted the Common Strategic Policy setting Council of Ministers' priorities until 2030, with four pillars including cost-of-living action. It passed 31 to 10 with two abstentions after backbenchers added a transparency priority, raising totals from 11 to 12. Chief Minister Lyndon Farnham praised the shared commitment and affordability focus, while Reform Jersey's Lyndsay Feltham argued rejected amendments on household affordability left real action missing.
items.title: Jersey Politicians Back Cost-of-Living Focus in Common Strategic Policy

items.summary: British cider makers warn that mounting alcohol duty, energy bills and packaging costs could force them to abandon home-grown apples. Matilda Temperley of Burrow Hill farm says a 61% tax rise by February would be tragic for orchards. Matthew Showering's firm grew from 80 to around 350 staff over ten years but prefers less government intervention, while Matt Gillett rejects importing pulp despite substantial duty costs.
items.title: Rising Costs Threaten British Cider Industry's Reliance on Local Apples

items.summary: U.S. lawmakers are advancing restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China, with bipartisan support growing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid a spy scandal involving an alleged romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese agent. House Speaker Mike Johnson noted increasing congressional consensus on limiting such exports. White House officials reportedly discussed whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should face removal as pressure mounts across Washington.
items.title: China's Nvidia Chip Access Faces Tightening U.S. Restrictions Amid Political Turmoil

items.summary: A fifth person, Shi Bingzhe (34), was charged on Nov 13 over an alleged fraud conspiracy linked to Nvidia chips. He faces 41 charges for allegedly consenting to money laundering by NJ Global Financial and Superphi, where he held senior roles. Four others were previously charged; six companies are also implicated.
items.title: Fifth Person Charged in Singapore Over Nvidia Chip Fraud Conspiracy

items.summary: The AI industry is grappling with uncertainty after Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia, the company dubbed the 'central bank of AI.' His abrupt resignation on Thursday followed revelations of multiple extramarital affairs and a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang had been a prominent champion of the sector across political and financial spheres. His departure arrives at a sensitive moment—just days before Anthropic's closely watched IPO amid growing concerns about the industry's massive investment spending.
items.title: AI Industry Weighs Future Without Nvidia's Huang

items.summary: NVIDIA's Board of Directors announced Thursday that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while continuing her role as executive vice president and CFO. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as NVIDIA CEO; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief Executive

items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce in Beijing said Thursday that China and the United States are maintaining close communication on implementing a reciprocal tariff-reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products from each side. Spokesperson He Yadong stated at a regular press conference that the arrangement would help stabilize and expand bilateral trade, raise business expectations, and create favorable conditions for agricultural trade.
items.title: China and US Maintain Close Communication on Tariff-Reduction Arrangement

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted email and online meetings across Australian schools, courts, government services, and health facilities starting just before 5am AEST on Friday. Reports peaked at 9.22am with more than 5,500 complaints of trouble opening or sending emails. The company said it had no indication of a cyber-attack, suggesting the issue stemmed from a server configuration change that overloaded systems. Federal officials confirmed their systems were affected but offered no details. Some hospitals reverted to paper for prescriptions due to authentication failures, while courts and supermarkets largely maintained operations. Experts compared the cascade failure to Optus's 2023 network collapse.
items.title: Australia Reverts to Pre-Email Communication Amid Major Microsoft Outage

items.summary: A global outage struck numerous Microsoft products used across hundreds of millions of workplaces, disrupting Outlook, Teams and Authenticator for Australian businesses, institutions and services. ABC IT discipline head Niusha Shafiabady warned that when systems fail overseas, Australian businesses feel consequences almost immediately, exposing reliance on technology the country does not control; smarter local systems remain useless if underlying infrastructure fails. The outage cascaded widely: stores lost email-based sales, patients lost telehealth access and long-distance schools shut for the day. In education, Melbourne student Emilie Yu said she could no longer study for her two remaining VCE language exams while teachers' help was inaccessible and the VCAA website had been down for the past two days.
items.title: How the Microsoft outage is affecting Australians

items.summary: A top national security official warned months ago that Australia's reliance on Microsoft risked disproportionate impact in the event of an outage. This warning was echoed by government agencies, including a review highlighting dependence on technology suppliers could threaten critical services. The Digital Transformation Agency commissioned a review of single-seller relationships, assessing them as rare but potentially catastrophic with medium overall risk. Several government agencies signed multi-year deals with Microsoft, including $720 million with Defence and smaller arrangements with Services Australia and the Australian Tax Office. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the government activated provisions in agreements to prioritize recovery from outages.
items.title: Australia's Reliance on Microsoft and National Security Warnings

items.summary: China's Foreign Ministry announced that President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held November 18-19 in Shenzhen under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." He will deliver remarks and hold a welcome banquet. The parallel APEC CEO Summit runs November 17-18 with its own theme; Xi attends its opening ceremony.
items.title: President Xi to Chair APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: Long before GPS, fishermen from Tanmen navigated the South China Sea using knowledge passed down through generations, recorded in Genglubu manuals that charted routes to distant reefs and fishing grounds. Some of these old captains also sailed to Huangyan Dao—internationally known as Scarborough Shoal. Their memories preserve a chapter of maritime life that is slowly disappearing.
items.title: The Sea We Call Home — Part Two: Our Ancient Routes

items.summary: A new report from the Schneider Electric Research Institute (SERI), released at UN COP31, models how solar paired with battery storage could reduce Europe's electricity system costs by up to 40 per cent in the 2030s. The study ran 40,500 scenarios across combinations of solar, battery and grid costs. SERI quotes Laurent Bataille: 'Solar is the fuel, the battery is the power plant.' Savings could add roughly 0.8 per cent to global GDP by 2030.
items.title: Solar and Battery Harmony Could Cut European Electricity Costs by Up to 40%

items.summary: EU leaders gathered informally in Dublin on Friday for their first artificial intelligence discussion, but the agenda was overshadowed by a dispute over who should represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks. European Council President António Costa added the issue after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that multiple EU formats made negotiations less credible. Costa put himself forward as natural representative; Luxembourg's Luc Frieden supported him, while foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas argued for her and Costa to lead on security. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged a decision by month's end. Germany defended the E3 format with France, UK, Poland and Italy. The summit also featured Mistral AI's Arthur Mensch and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton addressing Europe's AI competitiveness and existential risks.
items.title: Ukraine Envoy Row Hijacks EU Leaders' First AI Summit

items.summary: Poland's East Shield initiative aims to fortify its eastern border, but conservationists propose 'warwilding'—restoring forests as natural barriers. Scientists like Michal Zmihorski argue tanks cannot traverse dense woodlands, gaining military support from Marek Pietrzak. NGOs including PTOP rewild waterways amid drainage damage over 700 kilometers and road-widening threats across 2,000 kilometers.
items.title: Białowieża Forest Defense and Rewilding Efforts in Poland

items.summary: The FBI says state-sponsored hackers from North Korea stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency through a scheme called FaceStealer, which used fake video calls to steal identities. More than 900 victims were targeted in the last 18 months. The bureau links these thefts to Pyongyang's weapons funding and notes similar attacks on Binance.
items.title: FBI: North Korean Hackers Used Fake Video Calls in $400m Crypto Heist

items.summary: The briefing opens with President Donald Trump saying he may use military force against Iran "right now" if US allies and ships are threatened, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described a planned Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange as the largest of its kind. Israeli strikes killed 11 Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday, wounding around 40 others across Jabalia al-Nazla, near Al-Shifa Hospital, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged sustained effort to keep the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree target within reach at COP31.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 13

items.summary: On Friday (13 November 2026), South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reaffirmed his administration's commitment to capital market reforms, addressing domestic stock undervaluation he called an "unreasonable abnormality". Speaking at the Korea Exchange amid KOSPI volatility in the mid-5,000-point range—down from a late-June record of 9,114.55—he cited geopolitical tensions and urged restoring investor confidence through institutional reforms and intensified enforcement against unfair trading practices.
items.title: South Korean President Vows Capital Market Reforms and Crackdown on Stock Manipulation

items.summary: Luke J. Lindberg, the new WFP executive director, called for an end to fighting in Sudan during a visit to Goz Al-Salam Camp, where hundreds of thousands face famine. The WFP fed 4 million people in August but cut aid due to funding shortfalls, leaving 900,000 without help; it now seeks $520 million to feed 5.4 million through April 2027. Sudan's war since April 2023 has created the world's largest humanitarian crisis, affecting about 34 million people.
items.title: UN World Food Programme Chief Urges End to Sudan War Amid Deepening Famine Crisis

items.summary: At Arlington National Cemetery during a Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, a sentinel reprimanded a group including US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. The incident prompted the Pentagon to award Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal for his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. BBC's Bernd Debusmann explains why Hegseth's party was disciplined and the history behind strict rules governing visitor behaviour, emphasising the importance of maintaining silence at the tomb.
items.title: Military cemetery decorum behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand

items.summary: An ICICI Bank report warns that food inflation will stay elevated over the coming quarters, driven by a weak monsoon, low reservoir levels, and shortfall in the kharif season. India's retail inflation rose to 6.08% in October from 5.54%, with food prices jumping to 8.9% from 7.7%. The bank forecasts CPI of 5.2% for FY27 and 5.0% for FY28, expecting the RBI to raise rates by 25 bps in December.
items.title: ICICI Bank Forecasts Continued Food Inflation and Likely December Rate Hike

items.summary: A major global Microsoft outage disrupted Teams, Outlook, OneDrive and Copilot, affecting businesses across regions. Downdetector reported Outlook problems peaked at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT Thursday; no full restoration timeline was given. Air India rerouted emails to maintain service, kept support channels functioning within its usual 24-hour response time and assured passengers of continued monitoring.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Services as Air India Updates Flight Operations and Passenger Support

items.summary: Microsoft has acknowledged a widespread outage affecting Exchange Online mailboxes, incident EX1550543, which disrupted Outlook web and desktop access plus email send/receive. Teams messaging largely held while calendar features faltered; Copilot, SharePoint (Exchange-dependent), To Do, Defender Safe Links, Planner, Purview, Fabric and Graph were potentially affected with impact varying by location and account. Recovery measures proved ineffective as changes were 'not taking as expected,' prompting exploration of alternative capacity increases amid persistent traffic-management imbalances. No confirmed restoration timeline exists; users are advised to monitor service health pages for incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Status and Recovery Efforts

items.summary: A major global Microsoft outage began when automated health checks failed on certain servers, triggering their shutdown and placing strain on remaining infrastructure. Engineers restarted affected servers—each taking up to 30 minutes—but a configuration change attempt hasn't delivered results. The disruption stemmed from a core process becoming overwhelmed rather than traffic spikes or cyberattacks.
items.title: Failed health check, elevated load, server restart: What led to the Microsoft outage

items.summary: Under scrutiny for at least three affairs, including one with Alice Huang suspected of being a Chinese spy, Jensen Huang lost his forceful manner before leaving co-founded company Nvidia. After initially denying infidelity since late 2025, he admitted the relationship to general counsel Tim Teter on November 6, prompting an independent board inquiry led by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. With around 60 executives reporting directly to him and no succession plan in place, Colette Kress became interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a successor among figures like Lisa Su and Rene Haas; Huang is expected to testify before Congress.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Final Hours Before Leaving Nvidia Amid Affair Allegations and Board Inquiry

items.summary: On November 12, Representative Richard Neal and Senator Ron Wyden asked the Commerce Department to preserve records on an agreement allowing Nvidia to export H200 AI chips to China in exchange for a share of sales revenue. The lawmakers question whether the Trump administration used export controls, tariffs, and Nvidia's political contributions—including $26 million donated toward Trump projects—to exert influence over the company. They also examine Singapore-based customer Megaspeed, suspected of supplying advanced chips to Chinese authorities, despite intelligence concerns about its executive Alice Huang. The arrangement may have functioned as an unconstitutional export tax, with Nvidia and AMD agreeing to give 15% of China chip revenue in exchange for licenses.
items.title: US Democrats Probe Nvidia's China Chip Revenue-Sharing Deal and $26 Million in Political Donations

items.summary: Starting November 12, a major outage disrupted several Microsoft 365 services—Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint Online and OneDrive—leaving users unable to access email or workplace applications. Nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported problems at the peak, per Downdetector. Reactions ranged from jokes about a welcome break to speculation of a cyberattack; Microsoft has not attributed it to one. Laura Loomer called it a national security threat and urged canceling government contracts. Microsoft traced the issue to servers becoming unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks, with elevated load caused by reduced server capacity rather than increased traffic. Recovery efforts included pausing deployments, redistributing network traffic, restarting affected servers, and examining configuration rollbacks.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Outlook, Teams, Copilot; Users Joke, Some Suspect Cyberattack

items.summary: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan purchased Strancally Castle, a Gothic Revival residence in County Waterford, Ireland. The registered sale of the principal home and up to one acre of land totaled €51,171,155 on August 17, 2026; earlier estimates ranged from €20 million to €30 million, with total estate expenditure higher. The three-storey mansion spans roughly 16,000 square feet within a 440-acre estate overlooking the River Blackwater, dating back around 1830 and originally commissioned by John Keily. This acquisition adds historic European architecture to a portfolio otherwise centered on US properties in California, Hawaii, San Francisco and Washington, DC.
items.title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan Acquire Historic Irish Castle

items.summary: Hours after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid allegations of an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of intelligence ties, President Donald Trump called the departure "a horrible thing" and "so sad to see happen." Speaking on Salem News Channel and Truth Social, Trump defended Huang as an honorable man and AI ally. He endorsed Tim Cook—though no agreement was confirmed—as successor, writing "A Legend replaces a Legend." Meanwhile, Nvidia CFO Colette Kress serves as interim CEO. US officials have not established whether Alice Huang was a spy; the FBI continues its investigation.
items.title: Trump Reacts to Jensen Huang's Resignation Amid Spy Allegations; Endorses Tim Cook as Successor

items.summary: The Hindustan Times morning brief of November 13 rounds up major headlines across politics, national and international affairs, sports, entertainment and technology. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid allegations of a third extramarital affair with an employee. Delhi's air quality worsened to the severe category on Friday, reaching an AQI of 403 at 7:30 am per HT's dashboard and the CPCB. NCP president Supriya Sule ruled out merger talks between party factions. Microsoft experienced a major global outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, with Downdetector tracking around 2 lakh user reports near 1 pm New York time.
items.title: Hindustan Times Morning Brief of November 13

items.summary: A widespread Thursday outage disrupted Microsoft 365 services worldwide, blocking Outlook inboxes and affecting Teams and the Copilot AI assistant. Downdetector logged about 138,000 Outlook reports at peak before falling to roughly 34,000; some users were affected for more than five hours into Friday morning in India.
items.title: Global Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Outlook, Teams and Copilot

items.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang. The board appointed Colette Kress as interim CEO while searching for a successor.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid Affair Reports and Espionage Probe

items.summary: On Friday, Microsoft admitted its fixes for a global outage were not working as expected, hitting millions of users across Microsoft 365 services. In an X statement, the company said changes to improve serviceability failed to take effect and it was identifying alternate workstreams to increase capacity amid sustained traffic imbalances.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Deepens As Company's Fixes Fail To Work

items.summary: President Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico over a migrant caravan of nearly 2,000 people heading toward the US southern border. He blamed new caravans on Republican midterm losses and warned Mexican authorities, Texas Governor Greg Abbott, Border Patrol and ICE must stop them. Meanwhile, Democrats' gains raise questions about immigration enforcement as state attorneys general-elect consider dropping defenses of restrictive laws.
items.title: Trump Threatens To Double Tariffs On Mexico Over Migrant Caravan

items.summary: On 12 November 2026, Microsoft suffered a widespread outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot. The disruption reached at least 74 countries and territories, with Outlook reporting the most incidents. Engineers confirmed recovery efforts were not going as expected, prompting traffic redirections, paused deployments, server restarts, and new health-check methods. Root cause remains unidentified while updates flow through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot Services

items.summary: Immigration officials intercepted Rohana, an Indonesian citizen posing as Kolkata resident Li Kim Lien, at the Sonauli border on Nov 10 while attempting to enter Nepal. She carried forged voter ID, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards with conflicting details, plus passports showing dual identities and employment visas. Unable to speak Hindi properly, she claimed to lead a Kolkata NGO assisting Buddhist monks traveling to China; authorities say no Chinese government link is established as the investigation proceeds.
items.title: Indonesian Woman Interrogated at Sonauli Border Over Forged Indian Documents and Alleged Chinese Links

items.summary: The Delhi government alleges that unidentified persons are dumping dead fish into the Yamuna to damage its image ahead of Chhath Puja, prompting a request for an FIR. This political exchange follows BJP MP Manoj Tiwari's claim that pollution dropped by half over the past year and that people could once again celebrate Chhath Puja in the river. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj countered that the 26-km stretch from Palla to Wazirabad has historically been clean, even under his party's government.
items.title: Delhi govt alleges plot to dump dead fish in Yamuna ahead of Chhath Puja, seeks FIR

items.summary: Nvidia's board announced on 12 November 2026 that Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately, following allegations of a third extramarital affair involving another employee. Colette Kress was named interim chief executive officer while a permanent successor is sought. The resignation followed earlier admissions of relationships with Alice Huang and Kimberly Powell. Reports indicate Huang forfeited $108 million in unvested stock.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid Allegations of Third Affair

items.summary: On the shifting charlands of West Bengal's Teesta, landless migrants and elephants coexist amid climate-driven instability. Residents like Budharu Muhammed lease informal plots—15 bighas—to farmers displaced from places like the Sundarbans, paying ₹5,000–₹7,000 per bigha seasonally. Maljurias of male elephants increasingly forage in cultivated fields; researcher Avijan Saha estimates around 300 use his study landscape versus over 700 across the wider region. Movements track cropping cycles: maize draws them March to June, paddy later. Residents cope with watchtowers and drums but suffer crop losses without compensation since their occupation is unrecognised. The Teesta's rising riverbed, dams, erosion and forest loss reshape these transient lands, trapping families in precarious, undocumented lives.
items.title: Migrants and Elephants on a Transient Teesta Charland

items.summary: The Election Commission released draft electoral rolls showing voter increases of up to 3% across nine states and Union Territories following the special intensive revision. Goa led at 3%, followed by Rajasthan's 2.2%. Other regions recorded smaller gains, including Kerala (1.5%), Bihar and Tamil Nadu (1.8%). Draft figures for some areas remain below pre-revision counts. The exercise has drawn concerns over potential voter exclusion and political misuse.
items.title: Voter Rolls Rise in Nine States and UTs After Special Intensive Revision

items.summary: A military vehicle carrying Army personnel overturned during a training exercise and crashed into a tree, injuring seven people. The accident occurred while the group traveled from Golconda Army Camp in Hyderabad to Shabad town in Rangareddy district, Telangana. Two of the injured are reportedly in critical condition. They were taken to the Army Hospital in Golconda for treatment.
items.title: Army Vehicle Accident in Telangana Leaves Seven Personnel Injured

items.summary: PM Modi attended Bengaluru's Prasanthi Kutiram Golden Jubilee, highlighting global expansion of Ayurveda and yoga. Over 150 Ayurveda courses worldwide are recognised through agreements with 28 countries. Yogasana is now part of major sports events via the Ministry of AYUSH. Initiatives like the e-Ayush visa support cross-border patient travel. The address also emphasised preventive health integration following reports of significant poverty reduction.
items.title: Ayurveda and Yoga Expand Globally Under Modi's Recognition Push

items.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk claimed Thursday he was placed under house arrest by police ahead of Ladakh's council polls, alleging the move curtails his right to protest. He challenged a Section 163 order valid for 60 days and alleged social media suppression. Panchayat elections are set for November 21; eight Autonomous Hill Development Councils vote December 4. Civil society groups and MP Mohmad Haneefa have urged postponement amid harsh winter conditions.
items.title: Ladakh Activist Sonam Wangchuk Claims House Arrest Ahead of Council Polls

items.summary: Capital-market stocks in India are gaining momentum as equities rebounded from late October, driven by lower crude oil prices and funds rotating out of a faltering global AI trade. Analysts at Sky Links Capital Group and BofA Global Research see structural growth potential ahead.
items.title: India Equity Surge Brightens Outlook for Exchanges and Brokerages

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department banned fishing across coastal villages from Vembar to Periyathazhai after a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclone. Over 270 mechanised, 2,000 country and 5,000 fibre boats remain moored, affecting more than 50,000 fishermen in Tuticorin district. The India Meteorological Department warns squally winds may hit the Gulf of Mannar and Comorin on November 13-14.
items.title: Cyclone Threat Halts Fishing in Thoothukudi and Tuticorin
